q-104763.name: Question 1
q-104763.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $10$ to get rid of the decimals:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.6x & =-3.6 \\ 10\cdot (0.6x) & =10\cdot (-3.6) \\ 6x & =-36\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the equation using the multiplication principle, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & =-36 \\ \frac{6x}{6} & =\frac{-36}{6} \\ \frac{\cancel{6}x}{\cancel{6}} & =\frac{-36}{6} \\ x & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

q-180234.name: Question 4
q-180234.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $100$ to get rid of the decimals:

$$
\begin{aligned}-0.06t & =-6.6 \\ 100\cdot (-0.06t) & =100\cdot (-6.6) \\ -6t & =-660\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-6$ to isolate $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6t & =-660 \\ \frac{-6t}{-6} & =\frac{-660}{-6} \\ \frac{\cancel{-6}t}{\cancel{-6}} & =110 \\ t & =110\end{aligned}
$$

q-180238.name: Question 5
q-180238.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $100$ to get rid of the decimals:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.52t & =0.4t+2.4 \\ 100\cdot (0.52t) & =100\cdot (0.4t+2.4) \\ 52t & =40t+240\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the equation using the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}52t & =40t+240 \\ 52t-40t & =40t+240-40t \\ 12t & =240 \\ \frac{\cancel{12}t}{\cancel{12}} & =\frac{240}{12} \\ t & =20\end{aligned}
$$

q-51617.name: Question 6
q-51617.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $100$ to get rid of the decimals:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.35q-0.3 & =-1 \\ 100(0.35q-0.3) & =100(-1) \\ 35q-30 & =-100\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the above equation using the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}35q-30 & =-100 \\ 35q-30+30 & =-100+30 \\ 35q & =-70 \\ \frac{35q}{35} & =\frac{-70}{35} \\ \frac{\cancel{35}q}{\cancel{35}} & =-\frac{70}{35} \\ q & =-2\end{aligned}
$$
